---
title: "Name the Fears"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** none. **Objective:** name what worries you about LLM agents, and learn the habit that answers each worry.
**Time:** about 10 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim: nothing here depends on a tool version.</span>
:::

## Why start with fears

You do not have to like these tools. Many careful people in science are wary of them, and most of the wariness is reasonable.
This odyssey does not ask you to stop worrying. It gives each worry a **habit** that makes the risk smaller, so you can decide with your eyes open.

Each worry below is a real enemy in this land. Each has a counter-habit, and the rest of the odyssey trains them.

| The worry | The enemy | The counter-habit | Where you learn it |
|---|---|---|---|
| "It will stop me learning." | Learning-drain | Write it first, predict before you look, ask it to explain instead of do. | Biodiversity Reef |
| "It produces slop in bulk." | Slop-ooze | Small steps, tests before code, a review budget. | Sequence Maze |
| "It makes things up." | Mirage | Check against something the agent did not write. | Sequence Maze |
| "Someone else has to review all this." | Review-leech | Review it yourself first, say that you used an LLM, send small changes. | Biodiversity Reef |
| "It could delete my work or leak my data." | Data-wipe | Undo (git), permissions, a sandbox directory, no secrets in prompts. | Ancient DNA Crypt |
| "I do not understand what it did." | Black-box husk | Ask for a changelog and explain it back before you keep it. | Sequence Maze |

::: {.callout-note}
Sometimes the right answer is not to use an LLM at all. Part of the skill is knowing when.
:::

## Battle: name the counter-habit
